crontab-generator.title: Cron Expression Generator
crontab-generator.description: Build a cron expression by picking fields, with a human-readable schedule, upcoming run times and a cheat sheet of the five fields.
crontab-generator.ref-dayOfWeek: Field 5: day of week (0 and 7 are Sunday)
crontab-generator.ref-star: Asterisk: any value in this field
crontab-generator.ref-names: Weekdays and months accept English names (0=Sun)

seo.intro: Build a cron expression from the minute, hour, day, month and weekday fields, with a human-readable schedule beside it and a reference covering field order, special characters, system literals and common patterns.
steps: Set the five fields in order; an asterisk means any value, and ranges or steps can be written 1-5 or */5.
Use a preset to drop in frequent combinations such as every minute, hourly or Monday midnight.
Copy the expression into crontab -e or your CI config and check it against the described schedule.

faq.a: Classic cron numbers Sunday as 0, and many implementations also accept 7 for ISO compatibility, so the two are equivalent. Weekday and month also accept English abbreviations.

faq.q: What happens if day-of-month and day-of-week are both restricted?
faq.a: Standard cron treats the two as an OR when neither is an asterisk, so a job runs if either matches — the most common source of surprise.
The five-field syntax works in Linux crontab, but Kubernetes CronJob, Jenkins and friends may use six fields with seconds or their own extensions, so check the target product.

seo.intro: Pick the input format on the left and the output format on the right to convert and pretty-print between JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, CSV, Markdown, HTML and SQL. Comment stripping and folding only affect the output, never your source text.
steps: Paste the data or type it in the editor, then choose its format on the left.
Switch the right side to the target format; indentation and style re-apply instantly.
If you need cleanup, tick strip comments or fold everything, then copy the output.

faq.q: Will converting change my source text?
faq.a: No. Every cleanup and folding option applies to the output pane only, so you can keep retrying other formats against the same input.
JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, CSV, Markdown, HTML and SQL — any pair can be converted, and same-format pretty printing works too.
No. Parsing and conversion run entirely in your browser and nothing is persisted.
